_comment: OpenAI rate card for Codex, USD per MILLION tokens. Edit freely; no code changes required. IMPORTANT: this prices tokens at OpenAI's regular API rates, which is NOT what a ChatGPT subscription charges. The dashboard labels the figure 'API-equivalent' for that reason - it answers 'what would this have cost through the API', not 'what were you billed'.
_buckets: `cacheRead` is OpenAI's cached-input rate - a tenth of the input rate on GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.3 Codex, a twentieth on GPT-6.1 Sol. `input` is charged on the UNCACHED remainder only: the parser subtracts cached_input_tokens out of input_tokens, which OpenAI reports as a total including cache hits. Cache writes: OpenAI bills them at 1.25x input on its newer models (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol), and GPT-5.3 Codex lists none, so its write rates are 0. OpenAI has one write rate with no TTL split, so both cacheWrite entries carry it. Codex has logged cache_write_input_tokens as 0 on every event seen, so these rates change no figure today - they are here so one does if that ever changes.
_longContext: OpenAI bills a request whose prompt is over 272K input tokens (cached included) at 2x the input and cache rates and 1.5x the output rate, for the whole request. `longContext` on a model carries that rule; the parser decides each request from its own prompt size. GPT-5.3 Codex lists no long-context tier.
_promotional: GPT-5.6 Sol's rates are promotional, 'at least through November 21, 2026' per OpenAI. Re-check after that date; the standard rates were $5 / $0.50 cached / $30 output.
_fastMode: Fast/priority mode doubles these rates. Codex does not record whether a turn ran in fast mode, so everything is priced at standard speed; heavy fast-mode use would run higher than shown.
_aliases: Model strings that appear in the rollout files but are a job title rather than a model name. They are priced as the target but keep their own identity in the charts.
